caption: We're R5 000 a month into a deposit and R2 100 a month into takeaways. Which of those would you cut first?

slides.title:
How we're saving
a deposit on
R25 400 p/m
Living in Kuils River
slides.body:
Him 28, her 27
Living together, in her parents' backyard room
Jobs: Warehouse picker & hairdresser at a salon
Combined net: R25 400 p/m

slides.title: Deposit savings
slides.includes: A separate savings account, debit order on payday
slides.body: It leaves the day we're paid. If it sits in the main account it's gone by the 12th.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Shoprite, Pick n Pay, a Saturday market for veg
slides.body: Her mom cooks on Sundays and we don't count it. We should.

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: The backyard room, to her parents
slides.body: They offered free. We insisted on paying. It keeps it fair.

slides.title: Takeaways
slides.includes: Nando's, Uber Eats, the Friday kota
slides.body: This is the one we don't say out loud. It's R2 100. We checked.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: His mother in Mthatha R1 200, her gran R800
slides.body: Neither of us ever discussed it. It's just in the budget.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol & car insurance, cellphones, electricity share, funeral policy, stokvel, streaming
slides.body: The stokvel is R800 together. It pays out in December and has a name already: 'the couch'.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R25 400, after the R5 000 has already gone into the deposit account. It lasts us about a week.

slides.title: We stopped guessing
slides.body:
We uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction.

The takeaways number was a bit rude.

No bank login needed.
